sense: of an idea: strained, not natural

terms.grammar: participle of conquīrō used as an adjective
evidence: Quint. 9.3.5: figūrae (opposed to obviae dīcentī) (Lewis & Short)
Traupman p. 98: conquīsītum cōnsilium, a far-fetched idea
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “sought out, chosen, costly”; in Quintilian, figures of speech searched for rather than coming to hand, which is the sense of “far-fetched”. Traupman’s conquīsītum cōnsilium applies it to an idea.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 98, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
